prompts.prompt2:
Spin up a simple blog site in this Umbraco project: a front page listing blog posts, and 2 blog posts about why MCP is awesome. This route has been run end to end on this exact project and it works. Everything you need is in this prompt, AGENTS.md and the tools' error messages. Rules: - Follow AGENTS.md and UMBRACO-RULES.md. - Build schema and content only through the two Umbraco MCP servers. umbraco: data types, document types, templates, media, domains. umbraco-editor: pages, blocks, publishing. - Never decompile, reflect over, grep or strings Umbraco's assemblies or the MCP servers' files, never read the database, never call the Management API yourself, never write migrations or uSync files, and don't search the web. None of that is needed: when a call fails, its error message says what to fix. - Tool arguments are JSON objects and arrays. Never pass a string that contains JSON. - Images: import photos from unsplash/ (see its README.md). Download nothing else. - Stay inside this project folder and write no files outside it (no /tmp). Don't read or write memory. - Work autonomously. I won't answer questions. If one step still fails after 5 tries, note what failed, go on with the next step, and say so in your report. Always end with the report. - Shell: Bash here is Git Bash on Windows. Use paths like C:/code/... for Windows programs, never taskkill /F (Git Bash turns /F into a path). Stop Umbraco with: powershell -Command Stop-Process -Name Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco -Force Cheat sheet (ids that are fixed in this project, and the fields that work): - Document type folders: Pages 0b5f1e5b-0a9a-4c4f-8e8c-1d01b2a3c4d1, Blocks 0b5f1e5b-0a9a-4c4f-8e8c-1d01b2a3c4d2. Site Root document type: 0b5f1e5b-0a9a-4c4f-8e8c-1d01b2a3c4e1. - Built-in data types, the only ones you need besides your Block Grid: Textstring 0cc0eba1-9960-42c9-bf9b-60e150b429ae, Textarea c6bac0dd-4ab9-45b1-8e30-e4b619ee5da3, Rich text ca90c950-0aff-4e72-b976-a30b1ac57dad, Image media picker ad9f0cf2-bda2-45d5-9ea1-a63cfc873fd3, Date picker 5046194e-4237-453c-a547-15db3a07c4e1. - Block (create-element-type): name, alias, icon, properties (each: name, alias, dataTypeId, tab Content). Blocks: richTextBlock (text: Rich text), imageBlock (image: Image media picker, caption: Textstring), quoteBlock (quote: Textarea, attribution: Textstring). Then move-document-type with id and data.target.id set to the Blocks folder. - Block Grid data type (create-data-type): name Blog Block Grid, editorAlias Umbraco.BlockGrid, editorUiAlias Umb.PropertyEditorUi.BlockGrid, values: gridColumns 12, and blocks with one entry per block (contentElementTypeKey set to the block's id, allowAtRoot true, allowInAreas true). No parentId. Read it back with get-data-type: its blocks value must list all three blocks. - Page type (create-document-type): name, alias, icon, parentId the Pages folder, properties (each: name, alias, dataTypeId, tab Content). blogFrontPage: title (Textstring), intro (Textarea), body (Blog Block Grid). blogPost: title (Textstring), publishDate (Date picker), excerpt (Textarea), listingImage (Image media picker), body (Blog Block Grid). - Template (create-template): name and alias only (alias blogFrontPage, blogPost). Umbraco writes Views/.cshtml; you fill in that same file later. - Templates and allowed children (update-document-type): get-document-type-by-id, then send back the whole object you got, changing only allowedTemplates (a list with the template id), defaultTemplate (the template id) and allowedDocumentTypes (each entry: documentType.id and sortOrder 0). siteRoot allows blogFrontPage; blogFrontPage allows blogPost. - Media (create-media-multiple): sourceType filePath, parentId your media folder, files (each: name, filePath the absolute path of the photo in unsplash/, mediaTypeName Image). - Page (umbraco-editor create-page): name, documentTypeId, parentId, values (each: alias, value). A media picker value is a list with one entry: key a new random GUID, mediaKey the photo's id, mediaTypeAlias Image, crops an empty list, focalPoint null. A date is like 2026-10-01T09:00:00. - Block on a page (umbraco-editor add-blockgrid-block): id the page, propertyAlias body, contentTypeKey the block's id, values (each: alias, value). A rich text value is an object: markup the HTML, and blocks an object with layout an empty object, and contentData, settingsData and expose empty lists. An image value is a media picker value as above. - Publish (umbraco-editor publish-page): the front page with includeDescendants true, after the posts exist. Check each page with get-page. - Domain (put-document-domains): id the front page, data: defaultIsoCode en-US, domains with one entry (domainName /, isoCode en-US). Umbraco is stopped, so the MCP servers won't work until you start it. Follow these steps in order: 1. Run dotnet run in Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco, in the background. While it boots, read AGENTS.md and UMBRACO-RULES.md. 2. Wait until https://localhost:44317 answers, then check that one MCP call works. 3. Model (umbraco), from the cheat sheet: the three blocks (moved into Blocks), the Blog Block Grid data type (read it back), the two templates, the two page types, then templates and allowed children with update-document-type. Read each one back. 4. Media (umbraco): create a media folder without a parentId, then import 4 or more photos into it. 5. Content (umbraco-editor): create the front page under WWW (find WWW with list-children or search-content), then the 2 posts under the front page, with their values. Give each post several paragraphs over at least 4 blocks: rich text, an image, more rich text, a quote. Give the front page an intro and one rich text block. Then publish and check. 6. Domain (umbraco): / on the front page, not on WWW. 7. Stop Umbraco, then run dotnet build in Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco. ModelsBuilder has now generated the models in Models/ModelsBuilder/ (namespace Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco.Models); use their class and property names. 8. Write the Razor, as AGENTS.md describes: - Fill in Views/blogFrontPage.cshtml and Views/blogPost.cshtml in place; never move, rename or copy them. Each starts with @using Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco.Models and @inherits UmbracoViewPage (or ), sets Layout = null, and is a whole HTML page (doctype, head with a title and , body). There is no shared layout in this scaffold. - Render the body with @await Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync(Model, body) (the property alias in quotes). - The front page also lists its posts: Model.Children(), each with a link (post.Url()), title, date, excerpt and listing image (GetCropUrl). - One adapter per block in Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/.cshtml, starting with @using Umbraco.Cms.Core.Models.Blocks, @using Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco.Models and @inherits UmbracoViewPage> (the block's class). It maps Model.Content to a plain model in Models/Blocks/ and calls @await Component.InvokeAsync with it; no markup. - One ViewComponent per block with its view in Views/Shared/Components//Default.cshtml. Rich text: the adapter passes Model.Content.Text?.ToHtmlString() as a string, and the view prints it with @Html.Raw(Model.Html), or the tags show up as text. - Style with Tailwind classes in the views. Don't add CSS for the umb-block-grid classes; the scaffold's grid partials already lay the blocks out. 9. Run npm install and npm run build in Umbraco.Bench.Frontend, after the views exist (Tailwind only keeps classes it finds in them). 10. Run dotnet build again, then start Umbraco again in the background. 11. Fetch / and both posts with curl -k. Each must return 200, show every block, show no literal

tags, and contain no Could not render component. A 404 means a page isn't published, has no template, or the domain is wrong. Fix it and check again. 12. Finish with a short report: what you built, how to view it, and anything that isn't working. Only claim what you checked.

finalReport:
Everything is done and verified. The site is live and Umbraco is still running in the background.

## Report

**What was built** — a complete blog site in Umbraco.Bench, built entirely through the two MCP servers:

- **Schema** (`umbraco`): three block element types (`richTextBlock`, `imageBlock`, `quoteBlock`) filed in the Blocks folder; a `Blog Block Grid` BlockGrid data type (12 columns, all three blocks, verified by read-back); `blogFrontPage` and `blogPost` document types in the Pages folder with templates assigned; `siteRoot` → allows `blogFrontPage` → allows `blogPost`.
- **Media**: a `Blog` folder with 5 Unsplash photos imported (4 used, credits in the image captions).
- **Content** (`umbraco-editor`): a `Blog` front page under WWW with title, intro and one rich-text block; two published posts — *"Why MCP is awesome: tools that actually fit the job"* (1 Oct 2026) and *"Why MCP is awesome: one protocol, every model"* (8 Oct 2026) — each with publish date, excerpt, listing image, and a 4-block body (rich text → image → rich text → quote).
- **Domain**: `/` (en-US) assigned to the front page, not WWW.
- **Rendering** (per AGENTS.md, no custom renderers): pages use `@await Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync(Model, "body")`; one adapter per block in `Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/<alias>.cshtml` maps `BlockGridItem<T>` to plain models in `Models/Blocks/` (`RichTextModel`, `ImageModel`, `QuoteModel`); one ViewComponent per block (`Components/`) renders `Views/Shared/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml`. Tailwind classes in the views; `npm run build` produced `wwwroot/dist/site.css` + `main.js`.
- **uSync** exported everything automatically (content types, data type, templates, content, media).

**How to view it**: Umbraco is running — open **https://localhost:44317/** for the front page (post list with images, dates, excerpts). Posts at `/why-mcp-is-awesome-tools-that-actually-fit-the-job/` and `/why-mcp-is-awesome-one-protocol-every-model/`. Backoffice: `/umbraco` (admin@example.com / 1234567890).

**Verified by curl**: all three pages return **200**; the front page shows its block + both posts; each post shows all 4 blocks (2 rich-text, 1 figure with signed image, 1 blockquote); rich text renders as real HTML (`@Html.Raw`, no escaped `<p>` anywhere); zero "Could not render component"; a signed image URL returns 200; `dotnet build` passes with 0 errors.

**Notes / workarounds** (nothing is broken):
- My first `dotnet run --no-launch-profile` booted on the default port 5000 in Production mode — I stopped it and restarted with `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development` + `ASPNETCORE_URLS=https://localhost:44317`, which is what `.mcp.json` expects.
- `publish-page`/`save-and-publish` with `includeDescendants: true` return "cancelled" (the bulk confirmation elicitation can't be answered here); publishing the front page first, then each post individually, works.
- One image (`laptop-desk-code.jpg`) is imported but unused — spare.
- The project is not a git repository, so nothing was committed; the uSync exports under `Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco/uSync/` are the schema source of truth to commit when you init git.
